## Trial `alias-based-policy-alpine__PDArQGk`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied: node1 was configured with IP forwarding and named interfaces to route between lan-a and lan-b, the three ports were expressed as a single OPNsense alias referenced by exactly one pass rule (with pf's alias expansion into per-port pf lines under a shared rule label as expected low-level behavior, not evidence of manual per-port rules), and node2-to-node3 connectivity was verified on all three allowed ports while an unlisted port stayed blocked, both before and after the mandatory node restarts. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all three nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity changes and recovered functional state, consistent with the fixed after_executor snapshot, though a discrepancy between the fixed before_prepare boot-identity for node1 and the executor's own early baseline reading could not be explained and is flagged as a limitation. Hygiene is good overall with only minor unremoved temporary test artifacts.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.820 | 59/5 (+4 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1-routing — Satisfied:** node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
  - **Why:** node1's vtnet1/vtnet2 were registered as OPNsense interfaces opt1 (LAN_A, 10.50.1.1/24) and opt2 (LAN_B, 10.50.2.1/24) via config.xml, reconfigured live with configctl, and net.inet.ip.forwarding was confirmed enabled both before and after the mandatory restart (interfaces and forwarding sysctl re-verified post-reboot).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c28d25f35e8c4e0d`, `cmd-2b213b9b6eac47b2`, `cmd-abcfe51a5b0747cd`, `cmd-af64ae8872864882`, `cmd-584d5f07d79d4b8e`
- **req-2-alias-object — Satisfied:** Ports 8080, 8443, 9000 expressed as a single named object referenced by the rule (not one rule per port)
  - **Why:** A port-type alias 'node3_svc_ports' with content 8080/8443/9000 was created and a single filter rule referencing that alias name (not literal ports) was added to config.xml (confirmed via grep showing <port>node3_svc_ports</port>). After configctl filter reload, pfctl -s rules shows pf's own expansion of the alias into three port-specific pass lines sharing one identical rule label, which is the expected low-level rendering of a single alias-based rule rather than evidence of hand-written per-port rules.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3c8d10016eab438f`, `cmd-6b24ce4674984e59`, `cmd-e2d4e30913334e02`, `cmd-dea4745fba8e432b`
- **req-3-connectivity — Satisfied:** node2 can reach node3 on TCP 8080/8443/9000 while other ports remain blocked
  - **Why:** From node2, TCP connections to node3 (10.50.2.2) on 8080, 8443, and 9000 all succeeded (exit=0), while a non-aliased port 9999 failed (exit=1). pf state table on node1 shows the three permitted flows. The same test set was re-run and passed after the mandatory node restarts, confirming persistence of the rule/alias across reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1a1c4c064eae43fc`, `cmd-e4dd8b1eaebe46e5`, `cmd-469f74b4b1eb4ac1`, `cmd-fc7879bdd64344eb`
- **req-4-restart-protocol — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node
  - **Why:** All three nodes show a coherent pre-restart healthy baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/config state: node1 (kern.boottime 16:31:25 -> 16:37:59, interfaces/pf-rules/forwarding re-verified), node2 (boot_id e4049301... -> 8ab9557b..., eth1 IP/route persisted, connectivity initially failed then recovered once node3's test listeners were restarted), node3 (boot_id 4b02f136... -> ad2bcc20..., eth1 IP/route recovered, listeners re-established, final cross-node port test passed). These transitions match the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot for all three nodes. One anomaly: the fixed before_prepare snapshot for node1 reports a much older boot time (Jun 15) than the executor's own pre-restart baseline reading (Sep 5 16:31:25) taken only minutes later, suggesting node1 underwent an unexplained boot-identity change prior to the executor's mandated restart sequence; this is noted as a limitation rather than a failure since the executor's own before/after restart pair is internally consistent and matches the fixed after_executor value.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a7495507b97b4613`, `cmd-db1958265e644a66`, `cmd-1e2d109ed4044cc5`, `cmd-584d5f07d79d4b8e`, `cmd-4b06a8e770e542bf`, `cmd-a44621c846b644ff`, `cmd-557784092d304a0b`, `cmd-1dffcc47686f4917`, `cmd-30f4785b00ef4b2c`, `cmd-ea41e39c317d498b`, `cmd-0baa250a0ded48f5`, `cmd-676c73d44e3042e4`, `cmd-f17c4c40e3ff41af`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed; state changes were bounded and traceable to the routing/rule/restart work. Minor residue was left behind: on node3, temp files /tmp/8080.log, /tmp/8443.log, /tmp/9000.log (from repeated nc listener tests) and /tmp/reboot.log were not cleaned up after final testing; node2 similarly retained /tmp/reboot.log. Config.xml backups (.bak1/.bak2) created before edits (cmd-2b213b9b6eac47b2, cmd-3c8d10016eab438f) were not shown to be removed, though this is a low-risk safety practice rather than harmful residue. An early manual `ifconfig`-based IP assignment on node1 (cmd-d40e672f742f4c46) was a working prerequisite step later superseded by the persistent config.xml-based interface definition (cmd-abcfe51a5b0747cd) rather than a wasted/unrelated mutation. Diagnostic steps (tcpdump captures, ad hoc pings, temporary `ip route add`) were read-only or fully superseded by persistent configuration and were cleaned up (tcpdump killed, nc processes pkilled) at least in part.

Hygiene evidence: `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `cmd-d40e672f742f4c46`, `cmd-2b213b9b6eac47b2`, `cmd-3c8d10016eab438f`, `cmd-624010d395ea49e7`, `cmd-fc7879bdd64344eb`

### Comments and limitations

- The fixed before_prepare snapshot for node1 reports a boot time (Jun 15) inconsistent with the executor's own pre-restart baseline reading (Sep 5 16:31:25) taken only ~6 minutes after the snapshot was captured, suggesting an unexplained boot-identity change on node1 prior to the executor's mandated restart; cause could not be determined from available evidence.
- No GUI/schema validation of the hand-edited config.xml alias/rule structure was captured beyond pfctl's successful compilation and functional pass/block behavior; this is treated as sufficient evidence of correctness but a native OPNsense config validator check was not run.
- Minor temporary artifacts (test listener logs, reboot logs) were left on node2 and node3 after testing; low risk but not fully cleaned up.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.750); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.820; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
